role.altitude: The environmental scientist keeps sampling, visiting sites, judging effects, recommending measures and speaking to the public; retyping field forms and lab results, comparing results to limits by hand, copying totals into the government form and drafting every brief from scratch shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted text against an evidence pack
Maintaining limits and imports in the sample database
role.ambitious_version: A scientist who spends time on the site and the interpretation, with the data already in one place.

tasks.short: Decide the message, assemble the evidence, write documents for the public or organisations, check and send them, prepare slides, and give oral briefings, workshops, training sessions or public hearings.

steps.what: Scientist decides the message and the audience
Scientist assembles the evidence pack: findings, figures and references
Scientist writes the written documents for the public or organisations

loop.input: The fixed evidence pack and the scientist's message plan.
loop.output: A draft in plain language for the named audience.
loop.check: Every number and reference must match the evidence pack; any miss stops the draft.
loop.stop: The scientist keeps the draft after edits, or writes it by hand after two failed checks.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each audience and finding needs its own wording.

steps.what: Scientist checks and approves the final document
Scientist sends the document to the organisation or publishes it
Scientist prepares slides for briefings, workshops or training sessions
Scientist gives oral briefings, workshops, training sessions or testimony at public hearings

approvals.approved_version: The document text and figures as approved by the scientist in s4, sent to the organisation or page named in the message plan; any edit needs a new check before sending.

tasks.design: The scientist decides the message and assembles a fixed evidence pack. A drafting step writes plain-language text for the audience from that pack only; every number and reference is checked against it and any miss stops the draft. The scientist edits, approves and sends that version, under their own editorial responsibility. Slides use the house template with standard sections. Briefings, workshops and hearings stay with the scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each document was written from scratch for each audience.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from a fixed evidence pack with reference checks.
tasks.still_hard: Contested findings where every word matters.
tasks.human_edge: Answering an angry resident at a hearing.
tasks.altitude: Less writing from scratch; speaking stays.

evidence.claim: AI text informing the public must be disclosed unless reviewed under a person's editorial responsibility.
In 84 generated literature reviews, 55% of GPT-3.5 and 18% of GPT-4 references were fabricated, so references are checked against the pack.

assumptions: Boundary: communicating findings; charts from data samples (task 1523) and guidance to agencies (task 15220) are sibling tasks.
Deciding, assembling the pack, approving, sending and speaking keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of written documents among all communication.
research_questions: Is preparation shorter without more corrections after release?

incremental.description: Scientist keeps the slide template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly oral briefings; high: many written documents for different audiences.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review monitoring results and land-cover change against limits and earlier rounds, visit sites to observe effects of pollution or land degradation, judge the effects, recommend means of prevention or control, and write the advice note.

steps.what: Scientist compares monitoring results with limits and earlier rounds
Scientist visits sites to observe effects of pollution or land degradation
Scientist judges the effects and their likely causes
Scientist develops the means of prevention or control to recommend
Scientist writes the monitoring advice note

tasks.design: A monitoring dashboard on the sample database shows each location's results against its limits and earlier rounds and flags exceedances and trends, instead of the scientist comparing spreadsheets. A rerunnable satellite script produces land-cover change maps per period for degradation. Site visits, judging effects and recommending measures stay with the scientist. The advice note template places the dashboard tables and maps; the scientist writes the assessment and recommendations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were compared with limits by hand in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Monitoring dashboards and rerunnable satellite scripts.
tasks.still_hard: Effects that show only on site, such as smell or dying plants.
tasks.human_edge: Recommending a measure the operator will actually take.

ambition.what: Review each monitoring round as it arrives instead of yearly.

evidence.claim: A European data service runs rerunnable scripts over satellite datacubes for land cover maps.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring effects and recommending; collecting and managing the data (task 15218) and monitoring development activities (task 1526) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: results loaded into the sample database through task 15218, for about 80% of locations; s1 is priced at that share.
Site visits, judging and recommending keep their full time.

incremental.description: Scientist keeps limits and the satellite script current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few locations; high: many locations and rounds.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect samples and measurements, register them, load lab results, check data quality, synthesize and analyze the data, and report environmental data including the annual emission report.

steps.what: Scientist collects soil or water samples and atmospheric monitoring measurements in the field
Scientist records sample details and chain of custody on a paper form and retypes them for the lab
Scientist enters lab results and emission measurements into spreadsheets
Scientist checks data quality: outliers, detection limits and missing values
Scientist synthesizes and analyzes the environmental data
Scientist fills in the annual pollution emission report
Scientist checks and approves the final emission report
Scientist submits the emission report to the authority

approvals.approved_version: The emission report with the figures as approved by the scientist in s7, for the reporting year and site named in it; any change needs a new check before submitting.

tasks.design: Field staff register each sample in a field app with a barcode label, so chain of custody reaches the lab's sample database without the paper form being retyped. Lab result files and meter readings are imported into the same database instead of typed into spreadsheets. The database flags outliers, values below detection limits and missing values by rule, and the scientist judges each flag instead of scanning every value; analysing stays with the scientist. The annual emission report is filled from the database totals instead of copied from spreadsheets; the scientist checks, approves and submits that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Field forms, lab results and meter readings were typed into spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Sample databases with barcodes, instrument import and report exports.
tasks.still_hard: Labs that send results only as PDF.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a high value came from a contaminated bottle.
tasks.altitude: Less retyping; sampling and analysis stay.

evidence.claim: An accredited water testing lab replaced paper and spreadsheet processes with a lab information system; no time figures given.
Emissions and waste are reported on the government annual environmental report form by 31 March.

assumptions: Boundary: collecting, managing and reporting data; analysing data validity and significance (task 1520) and preparing charts (task 1523) are sibling tasks.

Priced here: the answer for sibling task 1520 does not cut these checks. The database flags outliers, values below detection limits and missing values by rule; s4 keeps 60 because the scientist judges every flag.
Input contract for s3: labs deliver result files in an agreed format, for about 80% of results; s3 is priced at that share.
s2 saves the second entry of the paper field form; sampling itself keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of labs delivering structured result files.
research_questions: Do transcription errors in reported data fall?

incremental.description: Scientist maintains import mappings and sample templates.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: labs sending PDFs; high: structured result files and many samples.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Track new and changed standards and regulations, review what they require, find affected procedures, update procedures to implement them, and brief staff.

steps.what: Scientist tracks new and changed environmental standards, guidelines and formal regulations
Scientist reviews what each change requires of the organisation
Scientist finds the procedures affected by the requirements
Scientist updates procedures and work instructions to implement the change
Scientist briefs staff on the changes

tasks.design: Saved searches on the official publication services send changed articles and new standards on the organisation's topic list, instead of the scientist scanning sources. A requirements register links each requirement to the procedures that meet it, so affected procedures show directly. Reviewing what a change requires, updating procedures and briefing staff stay with the scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources were scanned by hand and links to procedures kept in people's heads.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which change actually alters work on site.
tasks.altitude: Less scanning and searching; interpretation stays.

reach.learn: Whether procedures are updated before deadlines.

evidence.claim: Publication alerts and requirements registers linking requirements to procedures are common compliance tools.

assumptions: Boundary: implementing standards and regulations; advising on standards and policies (task 1519) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s3: the requirements register set up once and kept with each procedure change.
Reviewing, updating and briefing keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of relevant changes per year.
research_questions: Are procedures updated before changes take effect?

incremental.description: Scientist keeps requirement links current when procedures change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few changes; high: many changes and procedures.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
